title: Himalayan Hill Stations: Himachal, Uttarakhand, Kashmir and the East
seoTitle: Himalayan Hill Stations: Himachal, Uttarakhand, Kashmir
metaDescription: The Himalayan hill stations of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Kashmir compared: Shimla, Manali, Dharamshala, Mussoorie, Nainital, Kausani, Gulmarg and more.
description: A guide to the hill stations of the western and central Himalaya: Shimla, Manali, Dharamshala, Dalhousie and Kasauli in Himachal Pradesh; Mussoorie, Nainital, Ranikhet, Kausani, Lansdowne and Auli in Uttarakhand; and Gulmarg, Pahalgam, Sonamarg and Patnitop in Jammu and Kashmir, with how they compare, when to go and how to combine them.
dek: North India's hill stations sit in the foothills and middle ranges of the Himalaya, most within a day of Delhi. Here is how they compare.

hero.alt: Mussoorie on its ridge in the Garhwal hills, Uttarakhand

intro: The Himalayan hill stations of north India fall into three groups. Himachal Pradesh has the widest choice, from colonial Shimla to Manali and the Tibetan town of McLeod Ganj. Uttarakhand splits into Garhwal (Mussoorie, Dhanaulti, Lansdowne, Auli) and Kumaon (Nainital, Ranikhet, Almora, Kausani, Mukteshwar). Kashmir has alpine resorts built around meadows, such as Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg.
Darjeeling and Sikkim, also Himalayan, are covered in our Northeast and eastern Himalaya guide.
quickAnswer: The main Himalayan hill stations are Shimla, Manali, Dharamshala, Dalhousie and Kasauli in Himachal Pradesh; Mussoorie, Nainital, Ranikhet, Kausani, Lansdowne and Auli in Uttarakhand; and Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg in Kashmir. March to June and October to December are the best months; higher resorts often see snow from December to February. Avoid the heavy monsoon weeks, when landslides disrupt roads.
takeaways: Himachal and Uttarakhand towns are within a day's travel of Delhi.
Kumaon towns such as Kausani and Mukteshwar have some of the best views of Nanda Devi and the high peaks.
Kashmir's resorts are about meadows and forests rather than towns.
The monsoon (July to September) brings landslide risk to Himachal and Uttarakhand.
Snow is likely in higher resorts in mid-winter but never certain.

sections.heading: Combining Himalayan hill stations
list: Shimla and Manali, with Dharamshala or Kasauli added (six to eight days).
Mussoorie and Rishikesh, or Nainital with Kausani and Mukteshwar (five to seven days).
Srinagar with Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg (five to seven days).
Manali with Jibhi or Tirthan for a quieter second half.

sections.heading: Why these towns grew
paras: Most of these towns were developed in the 19th century as sanatoriums, cantonments and summer seats of government. Shimla was the summer capital of British India; Mussoorie, Nainital, Dalhousie, Kasauli, Lansdowne and Ranikhet grew around barracks, schools and churches. That history still shapes their Mall Roads, churches and colonial cottages, while older temple towns and villages sit around them.

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: Stay near Mall Road or the Ridge for walkability in Shimla, Mussoorie and Nainital, or a few kilometres out for quiet and views. Manali's Old Manali and Vashisht have cafés and guesthouses; the Kumaon hills have small resorts and homestays with Himalayan views. In winter, confirm heating and hot water, and check whether the road to your stay is cleared after snow.

sections.heading: When to go
list: March to June: pleasant days; busiest in May and June.
July to September: monsoon rain, landslide risk and cloud; the Kashmir valley and Lahaul are better choices.
October to November: clear, crisp and quieter.
December to February: cold; snow is likely in Gulmarg, Manali, Auli and higher parts of the Shimla hills, though it varies each year.

safety: Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road and weather updates, and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes and pass openings change; check the official portals before you travel.
Carry warm layers even in summer; nights in the hills are cool.
In winter, carry chains or hire local drivers used to snow and ice.
packing: Warm layers and a waterproof jacket
Gloves and a cap in winter

faqs.q: Which is the best Himalayan hill station?
faqs.a: Shimla, Manali, Mussoorie and Nainital are the most popular; Kausani, Dalhousie and Lansdowne are quieter.

faqs.q: Which Himalayan hill station is closest to Delhi?
faqs.a: Kasauli, Shimla, Mussoorie, Lansdowne and Nainital are all within about 300 to 350 km.

faqs.q: Is it safe to visit Himachal and Uttarakhand in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Heavy rain causes landslides; if you go, keep plans flexible, check road updates and avoid night driving.

faqs.q: Where can I see snow in the Himalayan hill stations?
faqs.a: Gulmarg, Manali (and Solang), Auli, Kufri and Narkanda are the likeliest in mid-winter.

faqs.q: How many days do I need?
faqs.a: Three to four days for one hill station, and a week to combine two or three.
